title: Aladdin and the Wonderful Lamp

full_text:
In a city of China lived an impoverished youth named Aladdin, the son of a poor tailor. A treacherous sorcerer from the Maghrib, disguised as Aladdin’s uncle, led him into the mountains, unsealed an enchanted subterranean cavern, and sent him down to retrieve a plain bronze oil lamp, giving him a magic brass ring for protection.

When Aladdin refused to hand over the lamp before climbing out, the enraged sorcerer sealed the cave!

Trapped in darkness, Aladdin rubbed the brass ring in prayer: an immense Jinni appeared, declaring: 'I am the slave of the Ring! Command me!' Aladdin asked to be returned to his mother.

Back home, while cleaning the dusty bronze lamp to sell it for bread, Aladdin rubbed the metal: a colossal Jinni of the Lamp appeared in smoke, roaring: 'Command me! I am the servant of the Lamp!'

Aladdin used the power with noble restraint: he fed the hungry, learned trade, and won the heart of Princess Badr al-Budur through chivalry, building a palace of marble and pearls in a single night.

When the African sorcerer returned disguised as a peddler, shouting: 'New lamps for old!' and stole the magic lamp, transporting the palace to Africa, Aladdin did not despair.

Using the Ring, Aladdin traveled to Africa, outwitted the sorcerer with the aid of the courageous princess, recovered the wonderful lamp, and flew the palace safely back to China!

Aladdin became Sultan, governing with justice and generosity, proving that courage, integrity, and pure love conquer the darkest enchantments.
moral: Humility, courage, and faithful devotion conquer the darkest sorceries and build an empire of justice.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Aladdin and the Wonderful Lamp"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
